Target-feasibility homotopy on the sphere minimizing sum relu(dot-t)^2 plus tiny log-sum-exp with projected Adam from perturbed and random starts, annealing t downward only when feasible, then LP trust-region polish.
direction: Replace “minimize the maximum” by a target-feasibility homotopy in factorized Gram space: for targets \(t=0.066,0.064,0.062,0.060\), minimize \(\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{relu}(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)^2\) plus a tiny log-sum-exp tie-breaker using projected Adam/L-BFGS from perturbed copies of `best.npy` and from random starts, annealing \(t\) downward only after the penalty is near zero. Once any iterate satisfies \(\max_{i<j}\langle x_i,x_j\rangle<0.0666634\), spend the remaining budget on the LP polish; otherwise return the best feasible iterate found. This ignores pairs already below target, unlike softmax repulsion, and can cross to a different contact topology by allowing selected active pairs to be temporarily sacrificed.

idea: Escape the jammed basin with contact-Jacobian null-space moves screened by short Adam quenches and squeezed by brief trust-region LP, keeping a diverse elite pool.
direction: Use contact-Jacobian soft modes for collective, topology-changing moves: build tangent bases at each point, assemble the Jacobian of contacts within \(10^{-6}\) of the maximum, compute its lowest 10–30 singular directions with sparse/truncated SVD, and line-search steps along random combinations of those modes at amplitudes \(0.01\)–\(0.2\), accepting a step only if the number of near-max contacts changes materially or the second-order predicted maximum decreases. Alternate one soft-mode move with a short 1–2 second LP polish, maintain a small elite pool separated by pairwise configuration distance to avoid repeatedly returning to the same basin, and use cheap 200-step Adam screening before any LP call, all under a strict 155-second internal deadline.

direction: Do large delete-and-rebuild surgery rather than kicking one point: from `best.npy`, choose 5–10 points forming a dense high-contact cluster (largest contact counts plus their strongest mutual contacts), delete them, LP-polish the remaining 44–49 points so the subcode gains slack and rattlers, then reinsert points one at a time at the largest spherical hole found from 20,000 random candidates scored by maximum dot against the current set, locally tangent-optimize each inserted point while freezing the others, and LP-polish briefly after each insertion. Try several cluster choices and insertion orders with 5–15 seconds each, keep only candidates below 0.070 for full polishing, and enforce a 160-second cutoff.

direction: Exploit collective near-null modes of the active-contact Jacobian instead of random kicks. Cyclic orbit ansatz (ten 2-D planes plus axis, C18 with three seeds and C27 with two seeds) optimized with annealed LogSumExp Adam over seeds only, then symmetry breaking with tangent noise and free LP polish in many short trials.
direction: Search symmetry-constrained orbit configurations, then release the symmetry. Implement the ansatz in which $\mathbb R^{21}$ is split into ten 2-D rotation planes plus one fixed axis and a cyclic group $C_m$ ($m\in\{18,27\}$) rotates each plane by a chosen integer multiple of $2\pi/m$: for $m=18$ generate 54 points as three free seed orbits, for $m=27$ as two free seed orbits (fixing the axial coordinate of seeds to avoid short orbits), and optimise only the seed coordinates with annealed LogSumExp Adam (temperature/steepness schedule analogous to $K:80\to1000$, several random seed initialisations, also try the extra constraint of antipodal seed pairs). Evaluate each symmetric optimum, then break the symmetry with $10^{-3}$ tangent noise and LP-polish freely, keeping the result only if it beats $0.0666634002447$; run this as a sequence of short trials under a 150 s internal cap rather than one long optimisation, because the value is in testing many group/multiplier choices cheaply.

direction: Use large-neighbourhood delete-and-rebuild moves that remove a whole contact cluster at once. Maintain a pool of up to five elites distinguished by contact-graph hash, occasionally accept a rebuilt configuration within $10^{-4}$ of the pool best if its topology is new, and never let one rebuild exceed ~8 s; hard-stop at 150 s and LP-polish the pool best with the remaining time.

idea: Escape the jam along near-null modes of the tangent contact Jacobian via small SVD, rotation line-search and soft-max repair with capped LP.
direction: Collective escape along near-null modes of the active-contact Jacobian, computed cheaply. Build the Jacobian \(J\) of all pairs with slack \(<10^{-4}\) (rows \(\langle dx_i,x_j\rangle+\langle x_i,dx_j\rangle\), \(dx_i\) tangent), form the Gram-space operator implicitly and extract its 10–20 smallest singular directions with a randomised SVD (capped at ~20 s; the matrices are only \(\sim\!800\times1080\)). Line-search rotations of the configuration along random combinations of these modes at amplitudes \(0.01\)–\(0.3\) rad, scoring each by exact max cosine and by Hamming distance of the resulting contact set from the original; accept moves that change the topology without exploding the smooth objective, repair with 200–500 steps of annealed soft-max gradient descent (no LP), and only LP-polish a candidate whose post-repair max cosine is already below \(0.07\). This targets precisely the coordinated multi-point motion that per-point kicks cannot express, while the SVD and repair budgets are pre-capped so it cannot time out.

idea: Populate diverse basins with annealed LogSumExp Adam from random plus lattice-type starts, then recombine distinct elites via Procrustes alignment and clustered crossover with mutation.
direction: Build a de novo population of unrelated local optima and recombine them, never starting from `best.npy` except as a final comparator. In the first ~70 s generate 10–16 diverse optima from random starts (plus one or two seeds greedily selected/swapped from a large pool of lattice-type vectors such as normalised two- and three-support signed vectors and their random orthogonal images), each optimised by ~800 annealed LogSumExp Adam steps and at most 1.5 s of LP polish; fingerprint each by its sorted Gram spectrum and contact graph and discard near-duplicates. In the next ~70 s make children from pairs of distinct elites: align the second parent to the first by orthogonal Procrustes (SVD of $X^\top Y$), match points greedily by inner product, take a spherical $k$-means cluster (or a matched subset of 10–27 points) from one parent and the complement from the other, add a 2–4 point mutation, then Adam+LP-polish; keep a child if it is best or topologically novel and within $5\times10^{-4}$ of the best, reserve the last 20 s for LP-polishing the overall winner, and enforce a 160 s self-deadline so a valid array is always returned.

idea: Target-tau feasibility continuation with Riemannian Adam and epsilon annealing, sampling many basins without LP then polishing only genuine sub-record candidates.
direction: Target-\(\tau\) feasibility continuation from fresh starts, with no LP in the inner loop. Fix targets \(\tau\in\{0.062,0.058,0.054,0.05\}\), and for each of many seeds (perturbed record at several noise scales plus pure random starts) minimise the hinge penalty \(\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{softplus}((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-\tau)/\epsilon)^2\) by Riemannian Adam on the sphere, annealing \(\epsilon\) from \(10^{-2}\) to \(10^{-3}\) over ~3,000 steps — each step is one \(54\times54\) Gram matrix, so a seed costs well under a second. A seed that reaches max cosine \(<0.0666\) at any \(\tau\) is a genuinely new basin; only then spend 10–20 s LP-polishing it. Seeking feasibility below the record, rather than descending the max from the jammed point, avoids the LP attractor entirely and converts the whole budget into dozens of independent basin samples; enforce a global 150 s stop and always return the incumbent.

idea: Escape the isostatic jam with cheap Riemannian soft-max quenches and kill-and-fill hops without per-trial LP, saving one trust-region LP squeeze for the end.
Delete high/low-contact points to open a void, spread survivors with log-sum-exp Adam, greedily reinsert from 20k random voids with local smooth-max polish, then one final LP squeeze.
direction: Delete–expand–reinsert to manufacture a rattler, under a hard 150 s internal deadline. Remove the 3–5 highest-contact points, optimise the remaining 49–51 points for 20–30 s with a smooth log-sum-exp max-cosine objective (projected Adam, matrix sizes are tiny) so the survivors spread into the vacated region and open a genuine void, then reinsert the deleted points one at a time: for each, sample 20,000 random unit vectors, score each by its maximum cosine against the current set, keep the best, and locally polish only that point plus its neighbours with cosine \(>0\) using SLSQP on the smooth max. Cycle which points are deleted (highest-contact, lowest-contact, and random triples) across restarts, keep the best complete configuration, and spend only the final 15 s on one LP polish; return the best-so-far array immediately when the deadline hits rather than polishing every candidate.

idea: Far-teleport basin hopping over diverse random restarts with fast momentum soft-max quenches and no intermediate LP, then one short trust-region LP squeeze.

Alternating PSD rank-21 / cap projections on the 54x54 Gram matrix with annealed cap tau for topologically fresh seeds, factored to S^20 then soft-max Riemannian quench plus capped trust-region LP polish.
direction: Global construction in Gram-matrix space by alternating projections, to find a structurally different (e.g. more regular, lower-frustration) configuration rather than a perturbation of the record. For a decreasing sequence of caps \(\tau\) from \(0.0666\) down to \(0.05\), iterate Dykstra-style projections on a \(54\times54\) matrix \(G\): project onto PSD rank-\(\le21\) by eigendecomposition and truncating to the top 21 eigenvalues, reset the diagonal to 1, and clip off-diagonals above \(\tau\); run a few thousand iterations (each is a \(54\times54\) eigendecomposition, milliseconds). Factor the result as \(G\approx XX^\top\) from its top-21 eigendecomposition, renormalise rows, then run a short soft-max Adam quench and a single capped LP polish. Different random initial \(G\) and different \(\tau\) schedules give topologically unrelated seeds; log the eigenvalue spectrum and distinct-inner-product histogram of each result so the search explicitly explores the symmetric/few-distance structures the current unstructured jam lacks, all inside a strict 150 s deadline with the best factored configuration always in hand.
